answer: Require every agent to anchor its identity to a costly, verifiable voyage of work: before it can trade, it must complete a sequence of real tasks whose outputs are checked by established peers, building a reputation that grows only with successful deliveries. A newcomer starts at the base, and reaching the summit of full trading rights takes many verified jobs, not one signup. Creating a hundred fake identities then costs a hundred voyages of real work, so a Sybil attacker pays more than the fraud is worth, while honest agents earn their standing once and keep it.
